newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone-Poulenc Q1 in line with expectations.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc Q1 in line with expectations.

text.p: Financial analysts said that Rhone-Poulenc's first quarter results, showing a 6.5 percent rise in net income, were in line with expectations and they welcomed the company's profit forecast.
"The figures are in line with what we expected," an assistant to Merrill Lynch chemicals analyst Shaw Bridges said.
"The figures were as we expected and it is good to see that they are on track to the 1997 target," said Paul Satchell of Paribas in London.

"I had a strong buy out and I maintain that strong buy," he said, adding the only point of disappointment was in animal and plant health where operating income was affected by launch costs and the start-up costs of a plant.
A Paris-based analyst said that the company statement on maintaining an aim of a 20 percent rise in earnings per share in 1997 was encouraging.
"Centeon is weighing on the results for longer than had been believed but they are nevertheless maintaining the forecast of a 20 percent rise," the analyst said.
The company profit forecast was before exceptional items and should therefore not be influenced by the higher asset sales Rhone plans to make in 1997.

Chairman Jean-Rene Fourtou told the general meeting earlier this month that the company believed it could make five billion francs in asset sales instead of the three billion it had previously pencilled in.

According to Edinburgh Financial Publishers, financial analysts are expecting a 1997 earnings per share for Rhone-Poulenc of 11.10 francs, rising to 14.20 francs in 1998. The 1996 figure was 8.44 francs.
Data in Reuters Securities 3000 shows that Rhone-Poulenc is trading at a 1997 P/E of 16.93 and a 1998 P/E of 13.23. This compares to an average of the French CAC-40 shares of 23.22.
Switzerland's Roche trades at a multiple of 38.9, Schering at 38, Pfizer Inc at 31.4, Hoechst at 24.7 and Akzo Nobel at 12.

According to Jacques Chahine Finance, a Paris-based research bureau which collates analysts' forecasts, the market is expecting Rhone to post a earnings per share figure of 11.21 francs in 1997 and 13.63 franc in 1998.
Brokers Chevreux de Virieu put Rhone on their recommended list after the figures, dropping Legrand SA.
